run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T09:48:28Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The alert is firing because requests to the /api/data route are failing end-to-end. Error-status spans on frontend-proxy's own operations ("ingress" and "router frontend egress") jumped from a baseline of ~2–8 per 10-minute window to 98.9 at 09:56 and peaked at ~953 in the window ending 10:05, and its access log shows repeated "GET /api/data ... 500 - via_upstream" responses while other routes (e.g. GET /api/products/..., POST /api/checkout) still returned 200. Inside frontend, every failing span is on GET /api/data, "executing api route (pages) /api/data" and the outgoing call grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, with identical counts and zero errors on the cart/checkout routes; the deepest observed failure is the ad service's own server span oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, which had no error before 09:56 and then failed at roughly 88% of calls (227.4 error vs 30.9 UNSET in the 10-minute window ending 10:05), coincident with ad pod log lines "Exception while executing runnable io.grpc.internal.ServerImpl$JumpToApplicationThreadServerStreamListener$1HalfClosed@..." that begin at 09:56:16. The ad pod and all otel-demo workloads are healthy at the Kubernetes level (running, ready, 0 restarts, all deployments 1/1), GetAds latency is unchanged before vs after onset, and the failing spans themselves are short (171.4 of 227.4 error spans ≤2 ms), so this is an immediate application-level failure in ad, not CPU starvation, timeouts, a crash or a traffic surge. The exact trigger inside ad (most plausibly the flagd fault-injection flag "adFailure", which is defined as "Fail ad service" in flagd-config and defaulted off) could not be verified from the available telemetry.

claims.text: frontend-proxy has STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans on both of its operations, "ingress" and "router frontend egress"; in the 20-minute increase windows returned for 10:10–10:12:30 the ingress error figure is ~519.8–523.8 against ~9,519.8–8,124.3 STATUS_CODE_UNSET (these are increase() values over 20 minutes, not request counts).

The per-service 10-minute error-span increase for frontend-proxy was 2.1–8.4 in every window from 09:32 to 09:55, then jumped to 98.9 in the window ending 09:56, peaked at 953.0 in the window ending 10:05 and was still 238.3 in the window ending 10:12.

frontend-proxy access logs between 09:59:22 and 09:59:59 repeatedly show "GET /api/data... HTTP/1.1" 500 - via_upstream ... frontend (with and without contextKeys), while in the same interval "GET /api/products/..." returned 200 and "POST /api/checkout" returned 200.

In the frontend service, STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans are confined to GET /api/data, "executing api route (pages) /api/data" and grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, whose per-window values are identical (e.g. 487.78 each in the window ending 10:05); GET /api/cart, POST /api/cart, POST /api/checkout, executing api route (pages) /api/cart and /api/checkout, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder all show 0 error spans.

The ad service's STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans are on span oteldemo.AdService/GetAds (0 before 09:56, 78 in the window ending 09:57, peak 493.3 in the window ending 10:05); its other operation flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream carries a constant ~1.05 error spans per 10-minute window throughout, including before the onset.

In the 5-minute increase series for oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, STATUS_CODE_ERROR first appears at the 09:57 sample (78) while STATUS_CODE_UNSET falls from ~230–245 per window before onset to ~30.9–35.6 after it; in the window ending 10:05 the values are 227.43 error versus 30.86 UNSET, i.e. errors dominate the call mix after onset.
The ad GetAds error spans are short: of 227.43 error spans in the 10-minute window ending 10:10, 171.43 were ≤2 ms, 189.71 ≤10 ms, 208 ≤100 ms and 222.86 ≤400 ms.

The ad GetAds duration distribution is essentially unchanged before and after onset: le=2.0 counts are 131.4–140.6 per 4-minute window at 09:40–09:50 and 122.3–142.9 at 09:55–10:05, and le=+Inf is 186.3–198.9 before versus 168.0–205.9 after, so there is no latency shift accompanying the errors.

The ad pod's container log contains "Exception while executing runnable io.grpc.internal.ServerImpl$JumpToApplicationThreadServerStreamListener$1HalfClosed@..." lines beginning at 09:56:16 (no line matching Exception/error/fail text appears before 09:56:16 inside the 09:54–09:58 window) and continuing past 10:03; 453 such lines matched in 09:40–10:12 and the pod wrote 1,961 log lines between 10:02:49 and 10:03:22.

Pod ad-554b849958-sk6fg in namespace otel-demo runs container "ad" with image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad, ready=true, restartCount=0, empty lastState and state running, i.e. no crash, restart or prior termination.

All 21 otel-demo pods are Running with restartCount 0 and start times between 09:18:12 and 09:20:06, and all 21 otel-demo deployments report 1 ready / 1 available of 1 replica, including ad, frontend and frontend-proxy.

The ad Deployment configures container resources limits cpu=50m / memory=450Mi and requests cpu=10m / memory=225Mi, and env FLAGD_HOST=flagd, FLAGD_PORT=8013, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad.

The flagd-config ConfigMap (data key demo.flagd.json) defines fault-injection flags including adFailure ("Fail ad service", defaultVariant "off"), adHighCpu ("Triggers high cpu load in the ad service", "off"), adManualGc ("Triggers full manual garbage collections in the ad service", "off"), cartFailure, paymentFailure, productCatalogFailure and recommendationCacheFailure, all with defaultVariant "off".

Over the whole 08:48–10:12 window the per-service error-span enumeration returned series only for accounting (0), ad (475.6), fraud-detection (3.05), frontend (1956.6), frontend-proxy (1006.7), payment (0) and recommendation (3.05); no ERROR-status span series was returned for cart, checkout, currency, email, image-provider, kafka, load-generator, product-catalog, quote or shipping, so their error state is unknown rather than observed zero.

The only trace-derived metrics present are traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket; a name search matching http_server_request.* returned no such series, and separate searches for rpc_* / app_* metric names also returned nothing, so no HTTP/RPC server metrics or container CPU/throttling metrics were available for this analysis.

Root cause of the alert chain: the ad service's GetAds handler began throwing an application-level exception at 09:56:16, so essentially every frontend /api/data request fails its grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds call, frontend returns 500 for /api/data, and frontend-proxy records those upstream 500s as ERROR spans on its "ingress"/"router frontend egress" operations, which is what drives RequestErrorRate.

Most plausible trigger: the otel-demo fault-injection flag adFailure ("Fail ad service") was switched on in flagd at about 09:56 — the flag exists in the flagd-config ConfigMap, the failures are immediate rather than resource-driven, and no pod, deployment or image change occurred in the window; this is unverified because the runtime flag value and flag-change history could not be read.

ad GetAds latency did not degrade: its bucket distribution and the short duration of the error spans themselves (171 of 227 ≤2 ms) show the failures are returned quickly, which argues against CPU throttling, GC pressure or client deadline/timeout as the mechanism.

The ad container is ready with restartCount 0 and no previous termination state, and all otel-demo deployments are 1/1 available, so OOMKill, eviction, crash-loop or a rollout/reschedule does not explain the failure.

Other user-facing routes stayed healthy in the same minutes — frontend-proxy logged 200 for GET /api/products/... and POST /api/checkout while /api/data was returning 500 — so the failure is specific to the ad-dependent /api/data path, not a frontend-proxy or frontend outage.

The ad service's flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream error spans are constant (~1.05 per 10-minute window) both before and during the incident, so they are not temporally tied to the 09:56 onset and do not explain it.

Rejected: CPU starvation from the ad container's 50m CPU limit caused the GetAds failures. GetAds latency buckets are unchanged across the onset and the error spans complete in ≤2 ms 75% of the time, which is inconsistent with throttling-induced slowness or deadline expiry.

Rejected: a pod crash, OOMKill, eviction or controller rollout of ad explains the incident. The ad pod is ready with restartCount 0 and empty lastState, and the pod set and deployments were stable (pods started 09:18:12–09:20:06, all deployments 1/1).

Rejected: a traffic surge on the ad path caused the error spike. The GetAds error+UNSET total is not higher after onset (~200–230 per 5-minute window) than before it (~230–245), and the successful fraction collapses while volume stays flat or lower.

Rejected: frontend or frontend-proxy is the origin of the errors. The frontend's GET /api/data errors are exactly concurrent with, and numerically identical to, its outgoing grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds client-span errors and to ad's own server-span errors, while other frontend routes and downstream calls show no errors.

Advisory: inspect flagd's runtime flag state and its change/audit trail for flag adFailure around 09:56 (the ConfigMap only holds the static default "off"), and, if fault injection was intentional, disable it after the experiment to clear the alert.

Advisory: capture the full stack trace of the ad service exception (the retained log lines only carry the generic gRPC "Exception while executing runnable ...HalfClosed" text) so the failing code path can be identified, and review whether the ad container's 50m CPU limit is adequate even though latency is currently flat.

gaps: No alerting rule was found in this Prometheus (list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate and with type=alert both returned no data), so the RequestErrorRate expression and the alert's reported value 2.1111111111 could not be verified; the reported firing time 09:48:28 also precedes the observable error surge at 09:56, and that discrepancy is unexplained.

Jaeger held no traces after roughly 09:32:34 (traces_search for frontend over 09:55–10:12 returned no traces, and the frontend-proxy trace search only returned spans starting 09:32:31–09:32:34), so span-level status codes, error messages and parent/child detail for the incident interval are unavailable.

The runtime flag state and flag-change audit are unknown: the flagd pod returned 0 log lines for 09:45–10:05, no flagd metrics exist here, and the change_history integration is not available; the ConfigMap read shows static defaults only, not runtime overrides.

The concrete exception type/message thrown by the ad service is not present in the retained log lines (only the generic gRPC text), and ad logs before 09:56:16 were not retained in the read window, so the pre-onset behavior rests on metrics alone.

No container CPU, throttling or memory metrics are exposed by this Prometheus (only traces_span_metrics_* and kube-state series), so the effect of the ad container's 50m CPU limit could not be measured directly; the unchanged latency distribution is the only available proxy.

frontend pod logs returned no lines for container "frontend" (0 bytes read for 09:55–10:00), so the frontend's own error text is unknown, and the Kubernetes events query for namespace otel-demo returned no items in the window, so no event-based confirmation of configuration changes exists.

Trace metrics carry the otel-collector pod in their pod label rather than the workload pod, so the ad errors cannot be attributed to a specific ad replica beyond the single existing pod ad-554b849958-sk6fg.

Error-state coverage for cart, checkout, currency, email, image-provider, kafka, load-generator, product-catalog, quote and shipping is unknown: the whole-window error enumeration returned no series for them, and absence of a series is not an observed zero.
next_steps: Check flagd-ui/flagd audit logs or the chaos-experiment record for a change to flag adFailure at about 09:56, and disable the flag if the fault injection was not intended.
Extract the full ad service stack trace (or temporarily raise the exception log level) around the next occurrence to name the failing code path.
Retrieve the Alertmanager rule definition for RequestErrorRate to confirm which metric and threshold produced the reported value 2.1111111111 and the 09:48:28 firing time.
Add container CPU throttling and memory metrics for the otel-demo workloads so resource-limit hypotheses can be measured instead of inferred.
